endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: the vendor should additionally disclose: Scope of autonomy: Which actions can the agent take without confirmation? Which require human approval?

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether requiring vendors to disclose unconfirmed agent actions, or to acknowledge the deployer's oversight authority in contract, reduces hidden autonomous functionality or preserves deployer control. The recommendation currently rests on a single governance framework that uses "should" language.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains no studies that test the practice and no studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated when no comparative or observational data exist. The recommendation therefore reflects expert consensus from one source rather than measured effects on vendor behavior, deployer control, or patient outcomes.

The only endorsement comes from the CHAI governance playbooks, which advise that vendors should disclose which actions an agent can take without confirmation and which require human approval. This is voluntary framework guidance and carries no enforcement mechanism. The contractual acknowledgment of oversight authority does not appear in the quoted endorsement text and has no cited source of its own.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare contracts with and without autonomy-scope disclosure and oversight clauses. Such studies would measure whether disclosed action lists match observed agent behavior in production, how often undisclosed autonomous actions occur, and whether deployers use the contractual authority to pause or modify agents. Descriptive audits of current vendor disclosures would also establish whether the hazard occurs and how often.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these patients have no data on whether disclosure requirements change vendor practices in their settings, where bargaining power in contract negotiations and staff capacity to review disclosures may differ from larger systems.
